paragraphs.text: i.e., O islanders (so the Hebrews called all that were beyond sea to them), with whom God, being about to contest, calleth for silence that he may be heard. The people of Rome could hardly digest a Sιωπησατε, or keep silence from their emperor Adrian, as too severe; {a} but when God thundereth it, men wriggle into their holes as so many worms.
paragraphs.anchor: Keep silence before me, O islands

paragraphs.text: Come as strong as they can into the court, with their best advocates and arguments, since they are to debate the cause concerning their religion.
paragraphs.anchor: And let the people renew their strength.

paragraphs.text: This is a wonderful condescension. En in quantum se demittat Deus!
paragraphs.anchor: Let them come near together in judgment.

paragraphs.text: {a} Dio in Adrian.
Who but myself? Which of your idols can boast of such a man as Abraham was, like as I can?
paragraphs.anchor: Who raised up the righteous man from the east?

paragraphs.text: Making him follow his call with a blind obedience, for he winked and put himself into God’s holy hand, to be led at his pleasure. He "knew not whither he went," {Heb 11:8} nor much cared, so long as he had God by the hand, or might follow him as a guide, step after step.
paragraphs.anchor: Called him to his foot.

paragraphs.text: Gen 14:14. His posterity also prevailed exceedingly. And thus God stoppeth the mouths of those idolaters who insulted over the Israelites, because afflicted and subdued by other nations, as Cicero doth in his oration for Quintus Flaccus, extolling therefore their idols above the true God.
paragraphs.anchor: He gave the nations before him.

paragraphs.text: He got an unbloody victory over the four kings, not losing a man of all those unexpert soldiers. This was a great mercy, if not a miracle. War is usually utrique triste; no matter who wins a sorrow, victory is oft like a golden fishhook, which, lost or broken, cannot be paid for with that it taketh.
paragraphs.anchor: He pursued them, and passed in safety.

paragraphs.text: Here the Gentiles should have answered for God, which because they did not, but were senselessly silent, therefore he answereth by a description of himself.
paragraphs.anchor: Who hath wrought and done it?

paragraphs.text: Giving them their being, and having them at a beck.
paragraphs.anchor: Calling the generations from the beginning.

paragraphs.text: πρωτος τε και υστατος, εν τε μεσοι σιν. This was anciently believed concerning God, as Plato {a} testifieth. A te principium tibi desinet. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: I the Lord, the first, and with the last.

paragraphs.text: {a} De Leg., lib. iv.
{b} Virgil.
The heathens were convinced by the former arguments, yet not converted; they were afraid, and yet they came together to confirm themselves mutually in their abominable idolatries.
paragraphs.anchor: The isles saw it.

paragraphs.text: As it were, to justify their idolatries before the Lord. Such is the desperate obstinace of obdurate sinners. Pharaoh menaced Moses, even during that palpable darkness. The Philistines were afraid when they saw the ark of the covenant brought into the field, and yet they encourage one another to fight against Israel. {1Sa 4:8-9} The thief on the cross was under the arrest of death, and yet railed. Felix trembled, and yet expected a bribe from St Paul. There is a cold sweat sitteth on all the limbs of Antichrist at this day, and yet they repent not of their idolatries, nor murders, nor sorceries, nor fornication, nor thefts, {Rev 9:20-21} but defend them all they can.
paragraphs.anchor: Yea, they drew near.

paragraphs.text: Thus those desperate idolaters did from the first. Eusebius {a} telleth us, that in the seventh year of Abraham, Ninus, the founder of Nineveh, set up an image of his father Belus, which was worshipped after his death. So did other princes, by his example, not moved with God’s mercies showed to Abraham, who worshipped the true God alone, setting up altars to him wherever he came.
paragraphs.anchor: They helped every one his neighbour.

paragraphs.text: {a} In Chron.

Because no small gain was brought hereby unto these craftsmen. {Act 19:24-25} The Jewish doctors tell us that Terah, the father of Abraham, was an image maker at Ur of the Chaldees, till God called him thence. Hyperius saith, that all these words are to be taken as pronounced with derision and contempt, that so the vanity of idols may the more plainly be perceived, since they have no more worth than is given them by their worshippers.
paragraphs.anchor: So the carpenter encouraged the goldsmith.

paragraphs.text: And it was for thy sake, and for thy settlement, that I have dealt so long with those odious idolaters, whom else I would not once look toward nor commune with, as he said, 2Ki 3:14.
paragraphs.anchor: But thou, Israel, art my servant.

paragraphs.text: This style was a higher honour to Abraham than if God had engraven his name in the orbs of heaven. {See Trapp on "Jas 2:23"} Hushai was David’s "friend," and Augustus vouchsafed to give Virgil the name of "Amicus." This was a special favour, but not like that in the text.
paragraphs.anchor: The seed of Abraham, my friend.

paragraphs.text: sc., In the loins of Abraham thy progenitor.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou whom I have taken from the ends of the earth

paragraphs.text: Called thee and culled thee out of the grandees of the Chaldees, the rich, the potent, and the honourable, separate from the common sort, setting thee above the kings of the earth. {Psa 89:27}
paragraphs.anchor: And called thee from the chief men thereof.

paragraphs.text: Cordialibus, ut ita dicam, verbls, Deus hoc eloquitur, - As long as a child hath his father by the hand, he feareth none. Quid timet hominem homo in sinu Dei positus? - What should he who lieth in God’s own bosom fear any man alive? Is not God’s presence security sufficient?
paragraphs.anchor: Fear thou not, for I am with thee.

paragraphs.text: I will, I will, I will. Oh the rhetoric of God! Oh the certainty of the promises!
paragraphs.anchor: I will strengthen thee; I will help thee, &c.

paragraphs.text: i.e., My righteous right hand, that shall right all thy wrongs.
paragraphs.anchor: With the right hand of my righteousness

paragraphs.text: These and the following precious promises the Jews misapply to the coming and kingdom of their Messiah, the Papists to their hierarchy. Let every true servant of God take them home as spoken to himself; every promise droppeth myrrh and mercy.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, all that were incensed against thee.

paragraphs.text: Heb., The men of thy contention - thy contendents, such as this eristical age hath more than a good many. By the Quakers’ wild fancies and rude practices we may see how cross-grained these people are in contradicting everything. Many men’s spirits, saith one, today lie like that haven in Act 27:12, toward the south-west and north-west, two opposite points.
paragraphs.anchor: Even them that contended with thee.

paragraphs.text: As a tender father taketh his dear child by the hand, in dirty or dangerous ways especially, lifting him over; so the saints are said to sit down at God’s feet, {Deu 33:3} or to stand between his legs, as little ones do.
paragraphs.anchor: For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand.

paragraphs.text: This is oft inculcated, for better confirmation and comfort. Our Saviour may seem to have hence his "Fear not little flock." It is no easy matter to cheer up afflicted consciences. Luther saith it is as hard a matter as to raise the dead. Hence this frequent "Fear not."
paragraphs.anchor: Fear not.

paragraphs.text: Traham, aut tribulam in omnem partem probe dentatam. Such as those eastern countries did use, to mash in pieces their rougher and harder fodder for their cattle, or rather to thresh out their harder grain with, {Isa 28:25; Isa 28:28} or to torture men with. {2Sa 12:31}
paragraphs.anchor: I will make thee a new sharp thrashing instrument having teeth.

paragraphs.text: Thy lofty and mighty enemies. This was fulfilled in the Maccabees, but especially in the apostles, subduing the nations to the obedience of the faith. See 2Co 10:4.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt thresh the mountains.

paragraphs.text: But find nothing in them of any solidity. The heart of the wicked is little worth.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt fan them.

paragraphs.text: As the sole doer of all; for it is he that subdueth the people under us, and doeth all our works for us. {Isa 26:12}
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt rejoice in the Lord.

paragraphs.text: When such as are "poor in spirit," sensible of their utter indigence, shall blessedly hunger and thirst after righteousness, showing themselves restless and insatiated without it.
paragraphs.anchor: When the poor.

paragraphs.text: None to be found in the doctrine of the Pharisees, philosophers, or friars.
paragraphs.anchor: And there is none.

paragraphs.text: Rather work miracles, as once in the wilderness, {Exo 17:6-7} than my poor people shall want necessary support and succour (help).
paragraphs.anchor: I will open rivers in high places.

paragraphs.text: That is, saith Lyra, I will give variety of graces to my people.
paragraphs.anchor: I will plant in the wilderness the cedar, &c.

paragraphs.text: {a} That groweth of itself in wild places, saith Diodate, to signify that the Church will always have worldly wild plants mixed and growing in it. Box is always green indeed, and full of leaves, but it is of an ill smell, et semen habet omnibus invisum animantibus, {b} and of a worse seed.
paragraphs.anchor: And the box tree.

paragraphs.text: {a} Per varia ligna varietatem gratiarum insinuat. - Oecol.
{b} Sphinx, Philos.

Heb., Lay. Lay it upon their heart, which natural men are very hardly drawn to do. The best are so backward, that an Ezekiel may hear, "Son of man, behold with thine eye, and hear with thine ears, and set thine heart upon all that I shall show thee," &c., {Eze 40:4} and Haggai calleth upon the good people of his time to "consider" and better "consider." {Hag 1:5; Hag 1:7}
paragraphs.anchor: That they may see, and know, and consider.

paragraphs.text: He had dealt with the heathens, and convinced them; now have at their gods: and their best proofs are called for.
paragraphs.anchor: Produce your cause, saith the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Your bony arguments, argumenta trabalia; but, alas! they had none such.
paragraphs.anchor: Bring forth your strong reasons.

paragraphs.text: Not the God of Jacob; for that was now the matter in question, whether he were God, or the heathen deities. And because they were silent, and to seek {a} of such arguments, he helpeth them to a couple.
paragraphs.anchor: Saith the king of Jacob.

paragraphs.text: {a} το ζητουμενον.

By such arguments as these, Cleanthes in Cicero {a} testifieth, though himself were a heathen, that the deity might he known. And whereas it may he objected that the Delphic devil had foretold things to come, it is answered, that the devil cannot foretell all future things, nor anything infallibly, and of himself; but either as it is revealed unto him by God, as was Ahab’s fall at Ramoth Gilead; or as he foreseeth it in the causes, signs, or prophecies of Holy Scripture, wherein he is not a little skilled.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them bring forth, and show what shall happen.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. ii. De Nat. Deorum.

This first argument is much insisted on. God alone can properly predict; and Testimonium divinitatis est veritas divinationis. {a} Cato Major was wont to say, that he wondered how one diviner could look upon another and not laugh, as knowing themselves to be no better than deceivers of the people.
paragraphs.anchor: Show the things that are to come.

paragraphs.text: Good to your friends, evil to your foes. This is the second argument, and it is unanswerable. If it be objected, that this the devil can do, and hath done, the answer is; (1.) that idols can do neither good nor evil, (2.) no, nor yet devils; but the good they do their clients is a mere magic, and the evil they do to any is by divine permission. See Cyprian’s Fourth Treatise, De Vanitate Idolorum. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: Yea, do good or evil.

paragraphs.text: {a} Tertul. Apol., cap. 20.
{b} Vide etiam, Aug. De Civlt. Dei, lib. ii. cap. 22, 25, &c.

Hence Paul took that assertion of his; {1Co 8:4} "we know that an idol is nothing in the world." For the matter of it, it is true, wood is wood, and stone is stone; but the relation and signification which is fastened thereunto, is nothing at all: all the being of an idol is nothing but the idolater’s imagination.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, ye are of nothing.

paragraphs.text: Or, Of the basilisk or viper; it will do you to death.
paragraphs.anchor: And your work of nought.

paragraphs.text: Papists, therefore, must needs be abominable idolaters. Dr Rainolds’s work, De Idololatria Romana, is yet unanswered. Weston writes that his head ached in reading it.
paragraphs.anchor: An abomination is he that curseth you.

paragraphs.text: Here God beginneth to prove that he can do both those things, whereof the heathen vanities could do neither. This one in the text is Cyrus, say some; Christ, say others, by whom God here foretelleth that he will punish his enemies, but do good to his Church and chosen.
paragraphs.anchor: I have raised up one from the north.

paragraphs.text: Or, Proclaim my name.
paragraphs.anchor: He shall call upon my name.

paragraphs.text: Who, besides myself, ever did or could predict such a thing? If any other hath done it, we will do him right, called him a god.
paragraphs.anchor: Who hath declared?

paragraphs.text: Or, I first said to Zion. I first brought her that good tidings by my prophets.
paragraphs.anchor: The first shall say to Zion.

paragraphs.text: None to say anything for these dumb idols, why I should not pass a definitive sentence against them. It is, therefore, this -
paragraphs.anchor: For I beheld, and there was no man.
Behold they are all vanity.

paragraphs.text: See Isa 41:24.
paragraphs.anchor: Their works are nothing.

paragraphs.text: Or, Emptiness; Heb., Tohu. Nothing in themselves, and yet of sufficient efficacy to inflict vengeance on their worshippers.
paragraphs.anchor: Are wind and confusion.
